trajectory_summary: The call moves from a misconception-driven opener through a real friction point (ground-mount unavailable) and a sustained safety-liability line of questioning that the rep never fully resolves, before settling into a smooth, low-resistance booking close once the bill amount surfaces. The appointment gets set, but it rests on an unresolved product-fit conflict and an unconfirmed credit qualifier, making the booking more fragile than the calm ending suggests.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; observed outcome is a booked phone appointment for tomorrow at noon, but Stewart flags this as fragile given the ground-mount disqualifier was disclosed but not resolved with the customer's stated fire-safety objection to roof-mount.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: So, unfortunately, we're we're not able to do ground mount systems anymore.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer's core stated reason for wanting ground mount (fear of roof panels causing fire) is never revisited after the rep rules out ground mount, so the appointment gets booked without confirming Barry will actually accept a roof-mount system — this is the single biggest fragility risk in the booking.

key_moments.quote: So, unfortunately, we're we're not able to do ground mount systems anymore.

This leaves a live product-fit conflict baked into the booked appointment.
